If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.67 over 2 consecutive days), apply a 2–3% downward correction to forecast at day 16–30 to dampen volatility overreaction.  
When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day for late horizon (16–30) to prevent momentum overfitting.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is below 70% of recent high, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for early horizon (1–7) to capture sentiment-driven breakout potential.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is above 70% of recent low, apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias for mid horizon (8–15) to avoid false recovery signals.
